run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T05:12:05Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on frontend is explained by a rollout restart of the ad Deployment at 2026-11-17T05:10:54Z. The ad Deployment's pod template carries the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:10:54Z and its generation is 2; the controller scaled new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 from 0 to 1, started pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz, and scaled the old ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0, deleting pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq (events at 05:10:54–05:10:57Z). The replacement ad container defines no readiness, liveness or startup probe, and its first log line 'Ad service starting.' appears only at 05:15:07.903Z; ad service spans disappear from ~05:12:30 to ~05:19:30. Exactly in that gap, frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR at ~1.5–1.97/s with their successful (UNSET) series at zero, and the errors propagate up frontend's own GET /api/data and page GET spans. The frontend error series falls back to zero by ~05:20, when ad spans resume. Facts show the frontend alert was driven by the ad rollout/restart gap; the exact reason the new ad process took minutes to serve is not established by the evidence (candidate: the 50m CPU limit throttling JVM startup).

claims.text: At 2026-11-17T05:12:05Z frontend had a STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate of 0.5/s against 44.57/s STATUS_CODE_UNSET, and frontend-proxy had a STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate of 0.237/s; other traced services showed 0 or ~0.004/s error rates (ad 0, checkout 0, cart 0, payment 0, accounting 0).

Frontend error spans in 04:55–05:30Z are concentrated on one dependency path: increase of 422.6 error spans each on GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data and grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, plus 15.16 on tcp.connect; every other frontend operation (GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/*, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) shows 0 error spans in the same window.

Frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans: STATUS_CODE_ERROR rises at 05:12 (1.07/s in the 05:11–05:12 minute), stays ~1.5–1.97/s through 05:19, and is 0 from 05:20; the STATUS_CODE_UNSET series falls to 0 from 05:13 through 05:19 and returns at 1.73/s at 05:20.

ad service span traffic runs at ~3.2–4.0/s until the 05:12 minute (2.0/s in 05:12), is exactly 0 from 05:13 through 05:19, and resumes at 4.13/s at 05:20 and 3.7–4.1/s at 05:21–05:23; ad STATUS_CODE_ERROR is ~0 across the window except 0.033/s at 05:06.

In the otel-demo namespace the events table returned nine events between 05:10:54Z and 05:10:57Z, all belonging to an ad Deployment rollout: ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 SuccessfulCreate (pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started), Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-d89765fb5 from 0 to 1', Deployment ad 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0', ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 SuccessfulDelete and Pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq Killing.

Deployment ad (generation 2, observedGeneration 2, 1/1 ready) carries pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T05:10:54Z and image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad; its container has readinessProbe, livenessProbe and startupProbe all null, with limits cpu 50m / memory 450Mi and requests cpu 10m / memory 225Mi.

Pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz logs exactly one line, 'Ad service starting.', timestamped 2026-11-17T05:15:07.903167388Z, and has no previous container instance; the same pod is listed Running, ready=true, restartCount 0, startTime 2026-11-17T05:10:54Z on node i-00afa9d1463304f93.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0 except fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-vzsmb (restartCount 1); frontend-675fd7b5c5-c8fk6 is ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-17T04:38:27Z, i.e. the frontend pod was not restarted during the incident.
frontend-proxy itself recorded error spans in 05:00–05:30Z: increase of 447.98 on operation 'ingress' and 423.65 on operation 'router frontend egress'.

In a sampled slice of 80 spans from 05:08:37–05:08:39Z, i.e. before the 05:10:54Z rollout, frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds client spans carried rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and matching ad server spans (operation oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, rpc.grpc.status_code=0) were present, so the frontend→ad path was working before the pod replacement.

The flagd-config ConfigMap (demo.flagd.json) currently has adFailure defaultVariant 'off', adHighCpu 'off', productCatalogFailure 'off', paymentFailure 'off', paymentUnreachable 'off', recommendationCacheFailure 'off' and cartFailure 'off'; adManualGc has defaultVariant 'on'.

Service ad selects opentelemetry.io/name=ad on port 8080/targetPort 8080, the ad pod template carries label opentelemetry.io/name=ad, and the ad Endpoints object currently lists only pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz at 100.96.1.122:8080 on node i-00afa9d1463304f93.

A cluster-wide query for NetworkPolicy objects in namespace otel-demo returned no items (total_items_processed 0), so no NetworkPolicy in that namespace was found to explain refused frontend→ad connections.

The new ad pod shares node i-00afa9d1463304f93 with accounting-58d4b6c958-fth2t, currency-5d455cf6f7-nkfgv, kafka-ff7884766-j2br4, product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-k82fl and shipping-75d58f5d84-c54qm, and at 05:12:05Z those services still had non-zero span rates (product-catalog 10.91/s, currency 1.59/s, accounting 1.14/s, shipping 1.71/s), so the node was not uniformly failing.

The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is caused by the ad Deployment rollout restart at 05:10:54Z: it replaced ad's only serving pod, and because the ad container has no readiness/startup probe, frontend traffic was directed at the new pod before its gRPC server was serving, producing tcp.connect/gRPC failures on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, which surfaced as error spans on frontend GET /api/data and the page GET and raised frontend's error span rate.

The ~8 minutes between container start (05:10:56Z Started event, pod startTime 05:10:54Z) and the first ad server spans (~05:19:30Z), with the first application log only at 05:15:07Z, may be JVM/ad startup throttled by the container's 50m CPU limit; the evidence does not establish the actual startup cost.

frontend-proxy's own error spans on 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress' are most likely reflections of failing frontend responses on the proxied path rather than an independent proxy fault; the individual HTTP status tags of those error spans could not be retrieved.

flagd-injected ad failure is not the cause: the adFailure flag's defaultVariant is 'off' in flagd-config, and during the gap ad emitted no server spans at all, whereas a fault handled inside ad would still have produced ad spans.
NetworkPolicy blocking between frontend and ad is not supported: a query for NetworkPolicy objects in otel-demo returned no items.
A node-level fault on i-00afa9d1463304f93 is not supported: other pods on that node (product-catalog, currency, accounting, shipping) kept serving with non-zero span rates at 05:12:05Z.

A frontend crash or a frontend-wide fault is not supported: frontend-675fd7b5c5-c8fk6 is ready with restartCount 0 and startTime 04:38:27Z, and frontend operations unrelated to ad (cart, checkout, product-catalog, recommendation) show zero error spans in the same 35-minute window.

The ad Deployment itself was not erroring on its server side during the incident (ad STATUS_CODE_ERROR ~0 for the whole window), and no Evicted, OOMKilled, Unhealthy or Failed events were returned for otel-demo; the ad container has restartCount 0. The observed failure mode is absence of ad spans plus refused/errored frontend client calls, not ad-side error responses.

Give the ad container a readiness probe (and/or a startup probe) so its pod is not added to the ad Service endpoints until the gRPC server accepts connections, and consider a rollout strategy that does not drop the only serving replica (e.g. maxUnavailable 0 with surge) for single-replica services.

Review the ad container's CPU limit (50m) and its startup time, since the replacement pod took from 05:10:56Z to roughly 05:19:30Z before producing server spans, and confirm whether that startup duration is normal for this image.

gaps: Kubernetes state metrics are not present in this Prometheus: queries for {__name__=~"kube_.*"}, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready{deployment="ad"} and kube_pod_container_info{pod=~"ad-.*"} returned no series, so the ad pod's readiness transition over time and an old-vs-new image digest comparison could not be verified.
Frontend container logs for 05:08–05:25Z returned no lines at all, so the frontend's own application-level error text and HTTP status codes for the failing route are unknown.

Tag-filtered trace searches for http.status_code="500" (frontend GET /api/data, frontend-proxy router frontend egress) and rpc.grpc.status_code="14" (frontend grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds) returned no traces, so the exact status tags and any error detail fields on the failing spans are not visible in this sampled Jaeger view.

The alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not found by list_prometheus_rules, so the alert's exact expression and its reported value 2.355555555555555 could not be reconciled with the measured 0.5/s frontend error-span rate at 05:12:05Z.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so what or who issued the kubectl rollout restart (the restartedAt annotation only records the time 05:10:54Z) is unknown.
There is no baseline of a previous ad restart in the window, so whether the observed multi-minute ad startup is normal for this image/settings is unknown.
Trace views are biased samples and span-metric counts are span counts, not unique request counts; the number of distinct failed frontend requests is unknown.
next_steps: Check cluster audit/change history for who or what patched Deployment ad at 2026-11-17T05:10:54Z (the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt change).
Add a readiness/startup probe to the ad container and verify rollout behaviour for single-replica services with maxUnavailable 0.
Measure ad container startup time and CPU throttling (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total) to confirm or refute the slow-start hypothesis.
Confirm with frontend application logs whether /api/data returned 5xx while GetAds was refused, to close the proxy/status-code evidence gap.
